question: Can the standard encoder-decoder, encoder-only, and decoder-only Transformer families be stated as compact, mathematically precise pseudocode that is useful to theorists and implementers without reproducing thousands of lines of framework code?

key_findings.claim: The report's main contribution is a common formal vocabulary and a stack of fifteen composable algorithms, not a new model or empirical result.
key_findings.evidence: It explicitly scopes itself to architectures and algorithms rather than results, defines notation for sequences, matrices, masks, parameters, and probabilities, and builds complete forward, training, and inference procedures from token/position embeddings, attention, normalization, and unembedding primitives.

key_findings.claim: The attention presentation exposes masking as the central switch between bidirectional, causal, and cross-attention rather than treating these as unrelated modules.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 4 projects primary and context sequences into queries, keys, and values, applies a mask to the score matrix, and returns the softmax-weighted values. Setting the context equal to the primary sequence and changing the mask yields unmasked or causal self-attention; keeping a distinct context yields cross-attention. Algorithm 5 parallelizes this operation across heads and projects the concatenation.

key_findings.claim: The three canonical Transformer families are represented as small changes in information flow and layer ordering.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 8 gives an encoder-decoder model with bidirectional encoder attention, causal decoder attention, and cross-attention. Algorithm 9 gives a bidirectional BERT-style encoder. Algorithm 10 gives a pre-normalized causal GPT-style decoder. The surrounding text also locates Gato and Gopher as modality or normalization/position variants of the decoder-only template.

key_findings.claim: Training and generation are made explicit as wrapper algorithms, which addresses a real reproducibility gap that architecture diagrams alone do not cover.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithms 11-13 define sequence-to-sequence, masked-language-model, and next-token objectives and parameter updates. Algorithms 14-15 define autoregressive sampling for prompted decoder-only and encoder-decoder models, including temperature and stop-token behavior. The paper argues that these interfaces are often where consequential but undocumented choices occur.

key_findings.claim: The report is a pedagogical abstraction, not an executable or fidelity-tested specification.
key_findings.evidence: No implementation-equivalence tests, reference outputs, unit tests, type checker, benchmark, or error analysis are provided. The training loops use per-example vanilla SGD while the text notes that practical systems use minibatches and adaptive optimizers; the practical-considerations section lists preprocessing, scheduling, regularization, parallelism, and prompting techniques without incorporating them into the algorithms.

key_findings.claim: Calling the templates BERT and GPT is useful shorthand but overstates exact historical fidelity.
key_findings.evidence: The BERT-style algorithm captures bidirectional attention and masked-token prediction, but the displayed procedure always substitutes the selected token with mask_token and omits the original 80/10/10 corruption mixture, segment embeddings, special sequence tokens, and next-sentence objective. The decoder template similarly abstracts away optimizer schedules, batching, dropout, parameter initialization, caching, and many implementation details acknowledged elsewhere in the report.

key_findings.claim: Later program-to-Transformer work supplies a stronger validation path for the report's formalization agenda.
key_findings.evidence: RASP defines a restricted sequence-processing language and relates programs to layer/head requirements; Tracr then compiles human-readable RASP programs into actual decoder-only Transformer weights. Those works do not replace a readable general model specification, but they demonstrate how a formal description can become executable and testable rather than remaining unaudited pseudocode.

method.core_idea: Factor the Transformer into typed mathematical primitives, compose those primitives into canonical architecture families, and wrap each family with explicit training and inference procedures under one notation system.
method.mechanism: Text is tokenized and embedded with position information; scaled dot-product attention maps query and context sequences through learned query/key/value projections, masking encodes permissible information flow, and multi-head attention concatenates parallel heads. Residual MLP and normalization layers form encoder, decoder, or encoder-decoder stacks. Cross-entropy objectives and autoregressive sampling wrappers specify how parameters are learned and outputs generated.
assumptions: A compact mathematical abstraction can omit systems details while remaining sufficiently complete for the report's intended theorist and from-scratch implementer audiences.
BERT, GPT-2/3, Gopher, and Gato can be usefully represented as small variants of three canonical templates.
Column-vector notation, one-based indexing, and global symbol tables reduce ambiguity despite differing from common tensor-library conventions.
Per-example SGD pseudocode adequately represents training even when practical optimizers, batching, schedules, and distributed execution differ.
Tokenization and data chunking can be specified independently from the neural architecture without hiding behavior relevant to most formal analyses.
Human inspection, rather than executable conformance tests, is enough to support the report's precision and completeness claims.

techniques.role: Defines sequence, tensor, masking, and parameter symbols globally so later algorithms share one mathematical interface.
Expresses self-, causal-, and cross-attention through one query/key/value routine and a mask argument.
Builds full models by calling compact token, position, attention, normalization, and unembedding primitives.
Makes encoder-decoder, encoder-only, and decoder-only information flow directly comparable.
Connects forward models to sequence-to-sequence, masked-token, and autoregressive cross-entropy training.
States prompting, temperature transformation, token sampling, continuation length, and termination behavior.
Moves optimizers, preprocessing, regularization, and scaling tricks into a practical-considerations boundary around the core algorithms.

evaluations.setting: Document-level coverage audit across the standard Transformer pipeline.
evaluations.metric: Presence of formal definitions for data representation, primitive layers, three model families, training objectives, and inference.
evaluations.result: Fifteen algorithms cover embeddings, attention, normalization, unembedding, forward passes, three training modes, and two generation modes in roughly fifty core lines for the decoder-only path.
evaluations.baseline: Fragmented prose, diagrams, and thousands of lines of framework-specific source code.

evaluations.setting: Empirical or executable conformance of the pseudocode to named reference models.
evaluations.metric: Numerical equivalence, task accuracy, unit-test coverage, type checking, or reproducible implementation results.
evaluations.result: Not evaluated; the paper explicitly presents algorithms rather than results and supplies no conformance suite.
evaluations.baseline: Reference BERT/GPT/Transformer implementations or known input-output fixtures, none of which are run.

limitations: Author-stated: the report covers formal algorithms rather than experimental results and leaves practical enhancements mostly outside the core specification.
Reviewer-identified: the pseudocode is not machine checked or executed against canonical implementations, so compactness and apparent precision do not establish correctness.

Reviewer-identified: named-model fidelity is approximate; BERT's corruption recipe and several input/objective details are absent, while modern decoder training and inference omit caching, batching, schedules, and distributed concerns.
Reviewer-identified: tensor shapes are more explicit than in much prose, but datatype, device, padding, batch, and broadcasting semantics remain informal.
Reviewer-identified: no controlled user study tests whether theorists or implementers make fewer mistakes using the specification.

Reviewer-identified: the 2022 snapshot predates major architecture shifts such as grouped-query attention, mixture-of-experts routing, state-space hybrids, long-context mechanisms, and contemporary post-training pipelines.
Reviewer-identified: the practical-considerations list is selective and cannot serve as a reproducible training recipe.
Reviewer-identified: no revision protocol or executable source of truth is provided for keeping the algorithms synchronized with evolving implementations.
failure_modes: An implementer can produce a numerically valid but historically non-equivalent BERT or GPT because omitted corruption, initialization, normalization, or optimization details matter.
A notation-level dimension error can survive peer reading when the algorithms are not type checked or covered by fixtures.
Treating padding and batching as incidental can yield attention leakage or incorrect loss normalization in a real implementation.
The simplified SGD loops can be misread as a performance recipe even though the report itself says Adam and other training machinery are normally used.
Model-family labels can hide consequential variants in positional encoding, normalization placement, attention sparsity, and modality-specific embeddings.
A static prose specification can become obsolete as production Transformer stacks evolve.
Excessive compression can remove exactly the edge-case behavior a formal analysis or faithful reimplementation needs.
reusable_insights: Specify an ML system at three layers: mathematical primitives, compositional architecture, and training/inference wrappers.
Represent attention variants with an explicit information-flow mask so architectural differences become auditable parameters.
Keep a complete symbol and shape table adjacent to pseudocode; notation is part of the reproducibility surface.
Do not call pseudocode complete until it is type checked and tested against a reference implementation on fixed fixtures.
Separate a minimal semantic specification from an optional fidelity profile for each named historical model.
Treat tokenization, corruption, termination, and sampling as algorithms rather than dataset or deployment footnotes.
Use program-to-model compilation, as in RASP/Tracr, to connect human-readable abstractions with executable validation.
open_questions: Can these algorithms be encoded in a proof assistant or typed array language and proven shape safe?
What is the smallest conformance suite that distinguishes the major Transformer families and catches masking or normalization errors?
How should a formal specification represent batching, padding, KV caching, sharding, and mixed precision without losing compactness?
Can model cards publish both a canonical semantic algorithm and a machine-generated implementation diff?
Which omitted details most affect theoretical conclusions about expressivity, optimization, or generalization?
Can formal architecture specifications be versioned automatically as executable libraries change?

competitive_landscape.title: Attention Is All You Need
competitive_landscape.relationship: The original primary specification and empirical validation of the encoder-decoder Transformer.
competitive_landscape.difference: It introduces the architecture with equations, diagrams, and machine-translation results; the reviewed report re-expresses it and later descendants as compact end-to-end pseudocode but contributes no new benchmark.

competitive_landscape.title: A Survey of Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: A broad taxonomy of architectural modifications, pretraining methods, and applications available before the reviewed report.
competitive_landscape.difference: The survey provides much wider variant coverage and research context; Formal Algorithms prioritizes a small canonical core, unified notation, and line-level pseudocode.

competitive_landscape.title: Thinking Like Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Defines RASP, a formal sequence-processing language whose programs expose computations realizable by Transformer encoders.
competitive_landscape.difference: RASP abstracts upward from model mechanics to algorithmic tasks and predicts layer/head needs; the reviewed report specifies general architecture and training mechanics but does not compile or empirically test its programs.

competitive_landscape.title: Tracr: Compiled Transformers as a Laboratory for Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: A later compiler from human-readable RASP programs to standard decoder-only Transformer weights.
competitive_landscape.difference: Tracr makes selected formal programs executable and yields ground-truth model structure, directly addressing validation and testability; it is not a comprehensive specification of learned Transformer training or modern model families.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Transformers: A Survey
competitive_landscape.relationship: Systematizes the large design space of efficient attention and Transformer variants around computational and memory complexity.
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies taxonomy and tradeoff coverage for variants deliberately omitted from the reviewed report's vanilla core, while offering less of an end-to-end formal algorithm template.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first essentially complete, precise, and compact pseudocode for Transformer variants, spanning components, canonical architectures, training, prompting, and inference in about fifty lines for the decoder-only path.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The report supplies a shared notation table and fifteen linked algorithms that cover a substantially broader lifecycle than a forward-pass diagram alone, while explicitly contrasting the result with prose and large source-code implementations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The contribution is a strong pedagogical normalization of known mechanisms rather than a scientific result, proof, or verified specification. Its novelty is most credible at the level of unified end-to-end presentation; the unqualified 'complete' framing is weakened by approximate named-model fidelity and the absence of executable conformance tests. RASP and later Tracr show a more testable formalization path for bounded computations.

reviewer_notes: Read all 16 extracted pages, including the complete algorithms, architecture descriptions, training/inference wrappers, practical-considerations boundary, references, and notation appendix. Related primary arXiv records for the original Transformer, survey literature, RASP, Tracr, and efficient-Transformer taxonomy were checked on 2026-08-23.
